question: Because every carbon along the chain already holds as many hydrogens as it can, a _____ packs tightly against its neighbours and leaves a membrane in a more ordered state.
questions: Nine randomised trials covering 13,532 people found no significant fall in mortality from cutting _____ intake, which is not the answer the food labels imply.
Invented in the early 1900s as a cheap stand-in for _____ from butter and animals, partially hydrogenated oil kept longer and survived repeated deep frying.
abstract:
A saturated fat is one whose fatty acid chains carry no carbon-carbon double bonds, every carbon being bonded to as many hydrogen atoms as it can hold, where an unsaturated fat has one or more. That single difference decides how the chains pack against one another, and unsaturated lipids tend to raise membrane fluidity while saturated ones promote a more ordered state. Cold reduces fluidity by pressing membrane lipids closer together, so organisms counteract it by varying the proportion of chains that disrupt the packing, unsaturated ones among them. Saturation and chain length are the two variables a cell routinely adjusts to keep membrane fluidity inside the narrow range it has to stay in. The difference tells in a kitchen as well as a membrane, and partially hydrogenated oils were developed in the early 1900s as a cheap replacement for butter and other animal fats.

Industry liked them because they are inexpensive, they extend the shelf life of processed food and they need changing less often than natural oils during deep frying. The process also yields industrially produced trans fat, estimated to cause up to 500,000 deaths a year and entirely replaceable. Since 2018 the World Health Organization has run a global elimination programme against it, and 43 countries have adopted best-practice regulations covering a further 3.2 billion people. Saturated fat itself is a harder case than the labels suggest: a meta-analysis of nine randomised trials with 13,532 participants found no significant difference in cardiovascular or all-cause mortality between restricting it and not, and concluded that restriction cannot be recommended at present. That is a finding about the trials rather than about food, and commentary on it argues the question turns on what the saturated fat is replaced by and which foods it arrives in.
